questions.ancestry: Package boundary in the pinned bytes; INHERITED. The package imports find_integer and identity only -- no engine, no ConjectureData. Nyx expects this to be the first Chop Shop organ shown to behave OUTSIDE its ancestor (P4).
questions.mechanism: A base class holds the current value, the predicate and a seen-set, and implements consider() (c01's shape). Subclasses supply left_is_better (the order for this type) and moves: Integer tries 0 and 1, masks high bits, squeezes to a byte, shifts right, subtracts multiples of 2 then 1, each adaptively via find_integer; Ordering tries the fully sorted sequence, then sorts growing regions from each index, then regions around a fixed centre; Collection tries the min-size all-zero value, deletes chunks from the back adaptively, delegates to Ordering, shrinks duplicated elements together, then each element with an element shrinker. run() is one step, or to a fixpoint if full=True.
questions.input: a value (int / sequence / collection with an element shrinker), a predicate value -> bool, type-specific constraints (min_size, key, to_order/from_order)
questions.output: the smallest value found satisfying the predicate under this type's order
questions.state: current value, seen-set, change count; nothing outside the object
questions.assumptions: that the moves listed are the ones worth trying (the Integer docstring guarantees only 0, 1, initial-1, initial-2); that the predicate is cheap enough to call O(log) times per move family; that the type's left_is_better is what the caller wants
questions.interface: Cls.shrink(initial, predicate, **constraints) -> value; classes are composable via delegate/call_shrinker (Collection calls Ordering and an ElementShrinker)
questions.fitness_value: MEASURED (standalone, no engine imported; nyx/specimens/hypothesis_shrinker/ablations/RECEIPT_N1_2026-09-11.json P-a1..P-a3): Integer 1000 -> 43 under n > 42 in 14 calls; Ordering [3,1,2] -> (1,2,3) in 1 call; Collection (5,7,9,7,1) under 'contains 7' -> [7] in 11 calls. Local minimum shown (N-b, P3): under 'n >= 1000 or n == 5', Integer stays at 1000 after 8 calls -- 5 is not reachable by its move set (0, 1, masks, shifts, multiples); the reachable control (n == 0) returns 0 in 1 call.
questions.failure_landscape: (a) move-set minima -- NOW MEASURED: N-b (5 unreachable from 1000); N-d at engine level: a non-monotone predicate (x % 7 == 3 and x > 100) ended at 283 and 325 for two seeds, minimum 101 not reached, and the seed-1 result differed between two runs of the same script (1291 then 283) while derandomize=True was stable (S-a); (b) run() without full is one step (unchanged); (c) delete-from-the-back; (d) duplicates to the same value.
questions.ablation: unknown -- designed and CHEAP: disable each move family in turn on a fixture and count predicate calls and the final value. P-a in ablations/ will run at least the baseline. Not run at CUT-1.
questions.decomposability: (1) the greedy base (c01 shape), (2) per-type move sets (Integer / Ordering / Collection / Float / Bytes / String), (3) the composition rules (Collection -> Ordering + element). Each move set is separately removable.
questions.composability: Any Prometheus minimiser over plain values; Proteus's H1 minimiser today reaches these only THROUGH the engine and the choice-sequence encoding; a direct call on a program tree with size_key as left_is_better would be a different composition (not proposed; noted).
questions.human_prior: Which moves are 'natural' for integers (bits, halves, small subtractions) and sequences (sorting) -- a programmer's model of simplicity, not a property of predicates.
questions.control: RUN: three positives, one negative (always-false), one local-minimum plant, one reachable control. First Chop Shop organ exercised entirely outside its ancestor. Ref nyx/specimens/hypothesis_shrinker/ablations/RECEIPT_N1_2026-09-11.json.
questions.cheat: Claiming minimality (the smallest satisfying value) rather than local minimality under the move set; Techne's receipt already separates SOUND from MINIMAL for this reason.
